entry.summary: Australians are generally admitted visa-free for tourism and business subject to the current reciprocity/entry-fee position; ordinary tourist permission is up to 90 days and may be extended.
entry.pre_arrival: Check Migraciones and the Argentine consular/entry-fee position, then prepare a Spanish purpose letter.
entry.max_stay: Tourist permission is generally up to 90 days and may be extended; TIE/residence categories can be more accurate for work.

tourism.detail: Argentina's migration pages describe tourist stays up to three months and the TIE system lists business and other short categories; Australians should confirm current fee/waiver treatment.
tourism.next: Check the current Migraciones entry regime and any reciprocity charge.

meetings.route: TIE 24H business or short business entry
meetings.detail: Argentina has an explicit electronic business category for habitual business/representative activity supported by a registered Argentine requester.
meetings.next: Ask the host whether Re.N.U.R.E. registration and TIE 24H are needed.

conference.detail: Attendance can fit visitor/business purpose; professional delivery and paid tasks are separately named in TIE categories.
conference.next: Label attendee, speaker, trainer and exhibitor roles.

unpaid-speaking.detail: The electronic-entry menu expressly lists remunerated or non-remunerated scientific, professional, technical, religious or artistic tasks.
unpaid-speaking.next: Use the exact host, dates and unpaid/expense arrangement in the application.

paid-speaking.route: TIE 24H or temporary residence for local professional work
paid-speaking.detail: Argentina's migration categories can cover paid professional/technical/artistic tasks, but a proper permission is not the same as tourist entry.
paid-speaking.next: Have the registered requester choose the short TIE or temporary-residence category.

book-launch.detail: Rights meetings can be business; paid readings, workshops, signings, royalties and local sales should use the professional/artistic and tax framework.
book-launch.next: Separate author activity from merchandise and retail.

ai-teaching.route: Scientific/professional TIE or academic host route
ai-teaching.detail: Short teaching can be tied to a university or professional invitation; recurring local employment needs residence/work status.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the institution to state whether the role is academic exchange, paid teaching or service delivery.

remote-work.route: Digital-nomad category listed in TIE 24H system
remote-work.detail: Argentina's electronic-entry menu includes digital nomads; current duration, evidence and whether a visa is needed must be confirmed for the passport and stay.
remote-work.next: Check the current DNM digital-nomad instructions and keep Argentine clients separate.

entrepreneur.detail: Founder and investor activity is a residence/company question; the visitor/business route only supports exploration and meetings.
entrepreneur.next: Choose the Argentine entity, investment and operating role before setting up locally.

trade.route: Business/TIE route; local import and fulfilment separate
trade.detail: Fairs, market studies and negotiations can use business categories; local selling, customs and service delivery add other permissions.
trade.next: Map importer, invoice, customs and on-site work.

artist.route: TIE artistic category or cultural host route
artist.detail: Argentina expressly lists artistic tasks, including non-remunerated work, in its electronic-entry menu; paid performance still needs exact classification.
artist.next: Have the producer state fee, venue, dates and union/rights issues.

mixed-mission.detail: Argentina's strength is a menu that names several non-linear purposes, but each trip still needs one accurate principal category.
mixed-mission.next: Build the Spanish schedule and ask the host to choose the TIE/residence path.

activities.note: checked is the oldest activity date; each activity keeps its own.
